title: ChatGPT and academic integrity: a case study of assessment vulnerability in biological and environmental sciences
abstract: This study reveals that current assessments in biological and environmental sciences are highly vulnerable to generative artificial intelligence (AI) misuse, which threatens assessment validity. ChatGPT-4 either outperformed or approximated students in exam-style testing and on some essay assignments but struggled with tasks involving data collection, collaboration, and presentations. The authors recommend redesigning assessments to require deeper reasoning, ethical engagement, and clinical or experimental application, alongside ongoing monitoring of AI capabilities and increased use of in-person exams.

title: Employing causality when teaching physiology: deriving the Wiggers diagram from scratch to build better student understanding of cardiac function
abstract: Prediction in physiology is the pinnacle of learning outcomes and depends upon comprehension of the biological, chemical, or physical causal links between mechanistic events. The challenge of creating essential cognitive frameworks within which students can successfully think and reason in physiology is to present complex topics in small logical units that do not exceed the working memory capacity. Here we describe how we would develop a logic-driven explanation using the classical Wiggers diagram.

title: Permission to feel: addressing feeling rules as a prerequisite to emotional intelligence skill development in undergraduate prehealth education
abstract: The exploration of cultural influences on prehealth students’ emotional expression behavior in education contexts brings awareness to potential targets of cultural reform efforts to increase social and behavioral professional skills development. Feeling rules in undergraduate prehealth education are examined and identified in this study. Results suggest that prehealth students perceive an emotionally unsafe learning environment, which may hinder emotional intelligence development. We advocate for research related to increasing social-emotional learning in prehealth education.

title: Moving beyond check-the-box attendance: a token-based approach to encouraging meaningful UTA session participation
abstract: This article describes a future-oriented token system used to encourage meaningful participation in undergraduate teaching assistant (UTA)-led review sessions in a large undergraduate physiology course. Rather than awarding points for attendance, students earned limited-use tokens by actively participating in two sessions. The approach shifted the incentive away from check-the-box attendance and toward proactive help seeking, repeated engagement, and collaborative learning.

title: Participation in a medical academic Olympiad is associated with high intrinsic motivation and positive perceptions of academic outcomes
abstract: This study provides the first empirical evaluation of a student-led medical Olympiad within undergraduate medical education. By analyzing responses from 677 participants, it demonstrates that such initiatives can foster intrinsic motivation and enhance academic outcomes. Although academic Olympiads are well established in basic education, their use and educational impact in medical training have been largely unexplored. These findings highlight the substantial educational potential of student-driven, competition-based learning environments in medical education.

title: Clerkship faculty perspectives on basic science integration during clinical training: implications for fourth-year physiology elective development
abstract: This study is among the few to use perspectives of clerkship faculty, those who directly observe students’ clinical reasoning, to evaluate basic science preparedness and integration during clerkships. Faculty reported strong support for basic science relevance but identified gaps in its structured integration and in students’ application of foundational knowledge. Findings highlight high-yield domains for reinforcement and demonstrate broad support for targeted fourth-year physiology electives, offering a data-driven model for strengthening vertical basic science integration.

title: Integrating experimental design and statistics throughout an undergraduate human physiology laboratory course
abstract: We describe a model for practicing applied biostatistics in an undergraduate human physiology course. Statistical reasoning is embedded in every activity and assignment. Experiments are aligned with a specific statistical analysis, reinforcing experimental design, hypothesis development, data visualization, and interpretation. Through scaffolding, weekly application, in-class activities, Excel activities, and a capstone project, students practice selecting and justifying statistical analyses in authentic contexts. This framework strengthens quantitative confidence and normalizes statistics as an essential tool.

title: Exploring Careers in Healthcare & Onward (ECHO): a community outreach program to promote health care career interest in K-8 students
abstract: Participation in early career-oriented interventions has the potential to increase health care career interest in elementary and middle school students. By engaging youth from the local community in health care hands-on, career-oriented learning experiences, such programs may be able to empower students from underresourced communities to consider the pursuit of future careers in health care.

title: Incorporating advanced neuroscience research in undergraduate neuroscience education
abstract: Rapid advances in neuroscience underscore the need to prepare students for a highly competitive academic and research environment. We report specifically designed short-term research projects implemented as practical components of a third-year undergraduate course. Within these projects, students review background literature, collect data, perform analyses, and present findings to address defined scientific questions. These practical components not only provide valuable insights into neuroscientific methods but also reinforce students’ understanding of the fundamental principles of neuroscience.

title: Don’t use Costanzo
abstract: A medical school faculty member deals with the blow dealt by a student’s public, all-caps dismissal of her physiology textbook.

title: A practical approach to estimate the potency of an antagonist in a functional experiment with isolated preparations of rat aorta
abstract: By utilizing phenylephrine and prazosin in isolated rat aortas, students can better understand the concept of antagonist potency. This activity provides a practical opportunity to discuss key aspects of cell-drug interactions, including efficacy and intrinsic activity, via parameters such as EC 50 , IC 50 , equilibrium dissociation constant ( K b ), and antagonist potency (pA 2 ).

title: From preparation to pedagogy: positioning virtual reality as a scaffold rather than a substitute in dissection-based learning
Pulse of Surgery: an immersive educational operating room experience for the community
abstract: Pulse of Surgery is a unique immersive experiential initiative for students and community members that integrates a live cardiac surgery complemented by real-time bidirectional engagement and discussions with the surgical team and fun hands-on educational activities. Overarching goals are to promote the health care fields, educate participants in strategies for maintaining cardiovascular health, and inspire the next generations to consider a STEM or health care career.

title: Effectiveness of practicing with an e-learning tool based on an error-driven learning algorithm in physiology education
abstract: We developed an e-learning tool conceptually based on error-driven learning and implemented it in a first-year physiology course. The tool was designed to support correction of incorrect recall through repeated corrective feedback. Using objective measures derived from student activity logs, we showed that the number of repeated practices was significantly associated with learning improvement and final examination scores, even after adjusting for baseline academic aptitude and initial accuracy. This approach may support introductory physiology education.

title: Effect of a 3-D cell membrane model combined with an interactive online platform on health students’ learning of cellular physiology
abstract: Cell membranes are invisible to the naked eye, yet vital to life. For health care students, understanding transport across membranes can be challenging. This study combined a 3-D puzzle model with an online platform to make these processes tangible and easier to grasp. Students who used this interactive approach improved their self-perception of cellular function, showing that playful, hands-on educational strategies can facilitate learning of complex biological concepts and promote greater engagement in the learning process.

title: Interactive visualization of enzyme kinetics: a shiny app for biomedical, pharmacology, and biochemistry education
abstract: Students often find enzyme kinetics difficult because mathematical models can appear disconnected from biological meaning. The freely available Kinetics Analysis App was created to help address this challenge. Through interactive visualization of four classical kinetic models, learners are able to explore parameter estimation and model selection in real time. This web-based tool supports active learning, improves confidence in data interpretation, and provides an accessible approach for teaching quantitative concepts in biomedical and pharmacological sciences.

title: Revealing the link between critical thinking disposition and learning approaches: a cross-sectional study among Chinese medical students
abstract: This study is among the first to examine how deep and surface learning approaches predict CT disposition in Chinese medical students. By integrating the R-SPQ-2F and the CTDI-CV, we not only analyzed the associations between CT dispositions and LA but also developed a regression model explaining 39% of CT variance. Our findings highlight that innovative activities and academic performance moderate the CT-LA relationship, suggesting actionable targets for curriculum reform.

title: Goat rib bone marrow thick smear preparation as a low-cost, ethical, and high-utility laboratory exercise for teaching hematopoiesis
abstract: The present model introduces an active, hands-on learning approach that moves beyond passive slide-based instruction by directly engaging students in laboratory preparation and microscopic analysis. It establishes a sustainable, low-cost teaching resource for physiology laboratories while effectively bridging theoretical concepts of hematopoiesis with their clinical and morphological correlates. Importantly, the method is scalable and well suited for institutions with limited infrastructure, enabling authentic laboratory-based learning experiences without reliance on scarce human samples.

title: Project-based learning to promote multidisciplinary integration and transferable skills in undergraduate biology students
abstract: How can we break down disciplinary silos in biology? This study presents a project-based learning model implemented over 3 yr with 675 students. By exploring concrete and authentic research topics, students combine multidisciplinary investigation with the development of key transferable skills including teamwork, scientific communication, and autonomy. A practical guide to transforming biology education and better preparing future physiologists for interdisciplinary challenges.

title: ECGSight: a digital caliper application for teaching electrocardiogram interpretation in undergraduate medical education
abstract: ECGSight is an open-source, interactive digital caliper application developed with R and Shiny for measuring ECG segments and intervals from digital ECG images. It restores active, measurement-based learning that is often lost when students rely on automated ECG interpretations on screens. By shifting ECG education from passive viewing to deliberate skill engagement, the tool helps students better understand ECG scaling, interval boundaries, and clinical variability in a digital environment.

title: “Gastrointestinal Circuit”: an active learning approach to enhance understanding of human digestive system physiology
abstract: Physiology education often faces challenges such as limited instructional time, complex content, and low student engagement, leading to high failure rates. This study introduces the “Gastrointestinal Circuit,” a low-cost, active learning activity using large visual materials and interactive tasks to enhance undergraduate teaching of gastrointestinal physiology. Seventy students from Nursing, Speech-Language Pathology, and Biological Sciences participated in a pretest-posttest design and opinion survey. Results showed significant learning gains (P ≤ 0.05), particularly in the areas of gastrointestinal hormones and the enteric nervous system, as well as high student satisfaction. Additionally, the 2023 cohort, which participated in the “Gastrointestinal Circuit” activity, outperformed the 2022 cohort, which received only traditional lecture-based instruction, on related exam questions (P = 0.0035). These findings suggest that the “Gastrointestinal Circuit” is an effective and engaging tool for improving physiology education, with potential for further refinement.

title: Bridging basic physiology and clinical reasoning: student perceptions of a case-based collaborative activity with AI support
abstract: This study describes a simple, reproducible case-based collaborative activity in an introductory undergraduate physiology course in which students were permitted to use AI tools while solving clinical problems involving membrane transport disorders. The activity was associated with stronger perceived links between membrane transport and disease, greater confidence in mechanistic explanation, and continued reliance on peer discussion for deeper understanding. These findings suggest that AI can support, but should not replace, collaborative learning in physiology education.

title: JANATO: a comprehensive approach to exploring anatomy learning experiences and academic development in undergraduate and graduate education in Brazil
abstract: This study presents JANATO, an anatomy course integrating theory, applied anatomy, human tissue dissection, and research experiences to address persistent challenges in anatomy education. By combining participant evaluations with a SWOT (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats) analysis from organizers, the study offers a dual-perspective assessment. JANATO enhances learner engagement while supporting academic and professional development among organizers. The results identify actionable improvements and can serve as a model for anatomy and related disciplines for training future clinicians and educators.

title: V Symposium on Updates in Nervous System Physiology and XIV Neuroscience Applied to Education Course (Brazil, 2025)
Editorial Board
A flipped physiology course positively impacted student success and perceptions of learning
abstract: Utilizing the frameworks of Bloom’s Taxonomy and Constructivism, a flipped classroom in physiology showed an increase in the percentage of passing grades compared to traditional pedagogy, and students demonstrated the ability to use prior knowledge on a novel task. Their satisfaction with the flipped pedagogy was mixed, but this was primarily due to factors such as video quality and test modality (which was not unique to the flipped classroom).

title: Engaging the powerhouse: mitochondrial biology learning through Minecraft
abstract: The Minecraft Mitochondrial World (MMW) is the first comprehensive tertiary-level cell biology learning environment developed in Minecraft Education Edition (MEE). We describe an innovative approach to designing and deploying a dynamic, interactive, and experiential mitochondrial learning experience in MEE. The approach includes sophisticated simulations to model cellular respiration. We further describe how the MMW’s design principles make complex mitochondrial biology engaging, understandable, and enjoyable for learners of diverse educational backgrounds and learning preferences.

title: A storytelling approach to type 1 diabetes mellitus community health education to promote early recognition in underserved populations
abstract: This study addresses a critical gap in type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) education by focusing on early symptom recognition rather than disease management after diagnosis. Using a storytelling-based community intervention, we demonstrated significant improvements in knowledge, awareness, and confidence among adults in underserved populations. Notably, no prior studies have evaluated storytelling to promote earlier identification of T1DM. These findings highlight an innovative, scalable approach to reduce delayed diagnosis and prevent life-threatening complications such as diabetic ketoacidosis.

title: Cellular and network mechanisms of spreading depolarization
abstract: This Staying Current article details the fundamental mechanisms of spreading depolarization (SD), a common central nervous system phenomenon rarely discussed in neuroscience curricula that is implicated in many neuropathologies, including mild and traumatic brain injury, migraine, and stroke. Therefore, incorporating SD into neuroscience education adds clinically relevant context that engages students and supports deeper understanding of foundational neurophysiology.

title: Public health frameworks increase student’s ability to propose solutions addressing health inequity
abstract: The present study finds that teaching methods from public health disciplines in the physiology classroom improve students’ understanding of how to develop ideas to reduce cardiovascular disease (CVD) inequities. Our data support the notion that a multidisciplinary approach on the part of the instructor, integrating disciplinary knowledge from outside of physiology, is an effective approach to enhance problem-solving skills regarding CVD in marginalized populations.

title: Exploring qualitative education research: a primer for physiologists
abstract: Predicting student outcomes only tells half of the learning story. To fully understand student learning, we must also understand their experience. This guide aims to demystify qualitative education research. From foundational theory to real-world examples, learn how to capture the “why” of student learning.

title: Integrating art and science in physiology education: a commentary on “ParasitoPhysioArt” from an Indonesian perspective
Beyond content mastery: integrating executive function training with core concepts as a neurocognitive scaffold for physiology learning
Diagnostic instruments in extended curriculum programs: a scoping review
abstract: We propose a framework for diagnostic instrument development that incorporates cultural appropriateness, to ensure that the instrument respects and aligns with cultural norms; contextual relevance, ensuring that the instrument is suitable for specific situations; persistence, which evaluates students’ ability to continue despite challenges; psychosocial skills, which assesses social and emotional competencies; life skills, which measures practical abilities needed for daily life; content knowledge, which evaluates understanding of specific subjects; and cognitive abilities, which assesses cognitive abilities.

title: BioQueer : educational narratives on sex and gender—a methodology for developing, implementing, and evaluating an instructional guidebook
abstract: This study evaluates the BioQueer guidebook, an educational intervention developed to improve undergraduate understanding of differences of sex development (DSD) and sex and gender concepts. With a one-group pretest-posttest design with ordinal analysis [cumulative link model (CLM)], results showed consistent increases in participant scores. Despite design limitations, findings support the guidebook’s clarity and pedagogical potential. This exploratory study informs future research, including a planned randomized controlled trial to assess causal effects in physiology education.

title: Designing a human-AI collaborative model for precision teaching in undergraduate physiology laboratory education: a modified Delphi study
abstract: This study develops a human-AI collaborative precision teaching framework for undergraduate physiology labs with a four-module model. Through a two-round modified Delphi study with 15 experts, the study established consensus on scientific validity, feasibility, phased AI implementation, teacher leadership, ethical safeguards, knowledge graphs, and targeted training. The framework offers a practical, ethically grounded roadmap integrating AI while preserving teacher agency, pedagogical integrity, and equitable student support.

title: Unraveling the enigma of digestion: a digital educational activity as a tool for teaching digestive system physiology
abstract: We present a novel teaching approach in the form of an innovative digital marathon that integrates active learning strategies with widely accessible social media platforms to support the remote teaching of digestive system physiology. This approach illustrates how interactive, low-cost digital tools can be structured to facilitate engagement and discussion of theoretical content in virtual or hybrid learning environments.

title: Blended active instruction and exam stress: what are we truly reducing?
Countercurrent multiplication revisited: key conceptual updates and framework expansion
abstract: This article makes three advances in renal osmoregulation education and research. It provides a classroom-ready diagram to teach the emergence of the corticopapillary osmotic gradient and refines key countercurrent multiplication (CCM) concepts from my prior work. It reframes the transepithelial osmotic difference (ΔOC) as a system-level parameter amplified cycle by cycle during CCM. It also expands the CCM–equilibrium renal osmoregulation framework by reconceptualizing renal osmoregulation as a more dynamic, physiologically plausible operating regime punctuated by CCM episodes.

title: GutDigest: a new game to enhance active learning and assessment of gastrointestinal digestion of macromolecules
abstract: We describe the development of GutDigest, a new online educational game, to enhance the teaching, learning, and assessment of macromolecular digestion, which is a complex topic in gastrointestinal physiology courses across various curricula of medical and health science programs globally. The game will be a useful revision resource for students and an assessment tool for tutors to gauge their knowledge after being exposed to preliminary teaching of the topic.

title: Physiology of menopause and the role of hormone therapy
abstract: Natural menopause remains underrepresented in medical curricula, leaving clinicians with gaps in reproductive-aging knowledge. This Staying Current article gives physiology educators an updated, evidence-based overview—covering hormonal regulation, STRAW/STRAW + 10 staging criteria, and the pathophysiology of vasomotor, genitourinary, mood, and sleep symptoms. It critically revisits menopausal hormone therapy, including lessons from the Women's Health Initiative, alongside nonhormonal alternatives, equipping instructors to strengthen curricula and advance patient-centered women's health care.

title: The creation of freely accessible cardiac physiology and anatomy educational tools: AR, VR, mobile applications, and the Atlas of Human Cardiac Anatomy website
abstract: This article presents a suite of free mobile, augmented reality (AR), and virtual reality (VR) applications developed by the Visible Heart Laboratories at the University of Minnesota. These applications leverage real human heart anatomical data and advanced three-dimensional (3-D) imaging to provide immersive simulations that enhance learning for students and professionals worldwide. Designed for broad accessibilities, these applications allow users to explore the intricacies of detailed cardiac anatomy in highly interactive formats including mobile devices and AR/VR platforms.

title: Teaching Contemporary Lactate Physiology: Why It Is Time to Retire “Lactic Acid”
abstract: The terminology used to teach physiology should reflect contemporary scientific understanding. Although decades of research have fundamentally transformed our understanding of lactate biology, the term lactic acid remains widely used throughout physiology education, textbooks, coaching education, certification programs, and public communication. Under physiological conditions, however, lactate—not lactic acid—is the predominant molecular species, and modern evidence recognizes lactate as an oxidative fuel, signaling molecule, and regulator of metabolism rather than a metabolic waste product. This Perspective argues that physiology education should preferentially adopt terminology consistent with contemporary lactate biology. We discuss the historical origins of the term lactic acid, summarize the scientific advances that have reshaped our understanding of lactate physiology, and propose a practical educational framework for communicating these concepts across diverse learning environments.
